![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14197487/assets/807e4e931a2872dd6d2a570547b75f68935b3ea761cfaa8cda279a0e194130f9.png)

The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[0,5].$ The graph of ${f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above, where the areas of the regions between the graph and the $x$-axis are $3$ and $5$ respectively (from left to right). Find the minimum value of $f(x)$ on the interval $[0,5]$ given that $f(0)=-10.$
question.worked_solution:
According to the candidates test, the minimum value of $f(x)$ on $[0,5]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval.

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (0,5),$ and ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at $x=3.$ Therefore, the candidates are $x=0,3,5.$

**Step 2**: Compute the value of $f$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) & =-10 \\ f(3) & =f(0)+{\int }_{0}^{3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-10+3 \\  & =-7 \\ f(5) & =f(0)+{\int }_{0}^{5}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-10+3-5 \\  & =-12\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the smallest value of $f$ from our candidates.

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{f}_{\text{min}}=min\{-10,-7,-12\}=-12.
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $f$ is ${f}_{\text{min}}=-12,$ and the value of $x$ that minimizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{min}}=5.$
